One night two young men from Egulac went down to the river to hunt seals and while they were there it became foggy and calm. Then they heard war-cries, and they thought: "Maybe this is a war-party". They escaped to the shore, and hid behind a log. Now canoes came up, and they heard the noise of paddles, and saw one canoe coming up to them. There were five men in the canoe, and they said: "What do you think? We wish to take you along. We are going up the river to make war on the people." One of the young men said,"I have no arrows." "Arrows are in the canoe," they said. "I will count how many there are." When they had counted them he said, "There are five arrows." "Good!" they said. "Sometimes we shoot one, and sometimes we shoot two." But, just as they were going to start, there came a loud noise behind them, and they said, "Wow! How scary! That must have been a bear!" One of the young men said, "I will go and get some sticks." When he had got some sticks he gave one arrow to each of the others, and they began to shoot.
They had not shot a single arrow when a voice came from the canoe, "Why do you shoot arrows at night?" "We thought it was a war-party," they said. "Where are the war-parties?" "They have gone to the sandbars." "But we are not war-parties; we are canoes full of young men." "Sometimes war-parties come in canoes." "That may be so," they said, "but we are not war-parties." "What is the difference between war-parties and not war-parties?" "The difference is that war-parties shoot arrows in the daytime, and not at night." "

Another version of the myth explains the origin of the war party. Long ago, two young men of Egulac went down to the river to hunt seals. As they were hunting, the weather changed and it began to snow. They took shelter in a cave and saw pictures on the wall of the cave. One of the pictures was of a war party. The young men decided to join the war party and went with them as they went up the river to attack the people.
